title: Martinez Names Portugal's 26-Man World Cup Squad — Ronaldo Makes History at Record Sixth Tournament; Diogo Jota Honoured With Symbolic 27th Place
detail: Portugal head coach Roberto Martinez unveiled his definitive World Cup squad on May 19, confirming Cristiano Ronaldo (41, Al Nassr) for a record-breaking sixth FIFA World Cup — making him the first player in tournament history to appear at six editions. The squad is formally a 26-player selection, but Martinez announced an exceptional honorary 27th place dedicated to the memory of Diogo Jota, the Liverpool forward who passed away before the tournament, as a tribute from the entire squad. Key squad inclusions: Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United), Bernardo Silva (Manchester City), João Neves (PSG), Vitinha (PSG), Rafael Leão (AC Milan), Gonçalo Ramos (PSG), Rúben Dias (Manchester City), Nuno Mendes (PSG), Pedro Neto (Chelsea). The squad also features four UEFA Champions League winners. Portugal face Group K opponents DR Congo (June 18), Colombia (June 22), and Uzbekistan (June 27). Ronaldo will serve as captain. His inclusion had been widely anticipated following consistent form for Al Nassr, but his age and the potential emotional weight of a farewell tournament add a significant narrative layer. The concurrent Adidas campaign imagery of Ronaldo and Messi has amplified the 'last dance' storyline for both legends. 23 days to the June 11 opener at Estadio Azteca.

media.caption: Cristiano Ronaldo confirmed in Portugal's World Cup squad — making history at a record sixth tournament

title: Scotland Names 26-Man World Cup Squad — First Tournament Since France 1998; Robertson Leads Clarke's Historic Selection
detail: Scotland manager Steve Clarke revealed his 26-man World Cup squad at 12 p.m. BST on May 19, confirming Scotland's return to the FIFA World Cup for the first time since France 1998 — ending a 28-year absence from the sport's greatest stage. Captain Andy Robertson (Liverpool, 92 caps) headlines the squad alongside Scott McTominay (Napoli), John McGinn (Aston Villa), and Ché Adams (Torino). Tommy Conway was ruled out through injury and replaced by Ross Stewart; Craig Gordon and Findlay Curtis were named in the goalkeeping group. Scotland are drawn in Group C alongside Haiti, Morocco, and Brazil — a formidable group that includes South American powerhouse Brazil. Their World Cup opener is June 14 at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts vs Haiti. Scotland's qualification came through UEFA's expanded pathway under the 48-team format, and the achievement has been greeted with extraordinary national pride — widely regarded as one of the most emotional stories of the 2026 build-up. This is Clarke's first World Cup as Scotland manager after guiding the team through multiple European Championship campaigns. The squad composition blends top-league players from England, Italy, Germany, and the Scottish Premiership. 23 days to the June 11 opener.

media.caption: Scotland names 26-man World Cup squad — first tournament since France 1998; Andy Robertson captains the historic return

title: Make-or-Break Day: Iran in Antalya With Zero US Visas — FIFA-Infantino-Taj Zurich Summit Tomorrow; Yahoo Sports: 'Meeting Could Decide Iran's World Cup Fate'
detail: As of May 19 — 23 days before the June 11 World Cup opener — Iran's full national team squad and staff are training in Antalya, Turkey, and not a single US entry visa has been issued to any Iranian player or member of the coaching staff. The decisive FIFA-Infantino-Taj Zurich summit takes place tomorrow, May 20 — the last formal diplomatic channel before the June 1 squad submission deadline and the June 11 kick-off at Estadio Azteca. Yahoo Sports described the meeting as potentially decisive for Iran's World Cup participation. FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafström and Iranian FA president Mehdi Taj held 'excellent and constructive' pre-Zurich talks in Istanbul on May 17, with Taj saying FIFA 'offered solutions' to all 10 of Iran's raised points — but explicit US visa guarantees were not confirmed publicly. Iran's 10 demands include: guaranteed visas for all players and support staff, respect for the Iranian flag and national anthem, and security assurances at airports, hotels, and en-route transit. Iran's Group G schedule at US venues remains unchanged: SoFi Stadium, Los Angeles (June 15 vs New Zealand; June 21 vs Belgium) and Lumen Field, Seattle (June 26 vs Egypt). Tournament base camp: Tucson, Arizona. Warm-up friendly: vs The Gambia in Antalya, May 29. The June 1 squad submission deadline gives Iran's government 13 days from tomorrow's summit to comply with FIFA's framework — or trigger an unprecedented withdrawal from a World Cup 23 days before the opening match.

media.caption: Iran trains in Antalya with zero US visas — FIFA-Infantino-Taj Zurich summit tomorrow could determine Iran's World Cup participation
